title: Body, illness, and the doctor
title_target: 邊度唔舒服呀？ — Bin1 dou6 m4 syu1 fuk6 aa3?
goal: Name body parts and symptoms, talk to a doctor and a pharmacist, give advice with 應該, and forbid things with 唔好.
bekal: name body parts and say what hurts with 痛
answer a doctor's questions about symptoms and how long
give advice with 應該 and 最好
forbid things with 唔好 and 唔可以
buy medicine at a 藥房

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — At the clinic
dialogs.intro: Andi goes to a clinic with a fever. A Hong Kong doctor's questions almost always come in the same order: what hurts, since when, other symptoms, allergies.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [邊度唔舒服呀|Bin1 dou6 m4 syu1 fuk6 aa3]？
lines.id: What seems to be the problem?
lines.literal: which — place — not — comfortable — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我頭痛|Ngo5 tau4 tung3]，[仲有啲發燒|zung6 jau5 di1 faat3 siu1]。
lines.id: I have a headache, and a bit of a fever.
lines.literal: I — head — hurt, also — have — a-bit — emit — heat.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [幾時開始㗎|Gei2 si4 hoi1 ci2 gaa3]？
lines.id: Since when?
lines.literal: what — time — open — start — emphasis.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [前日開始|Cin4 jat6 hoi1 ci2]。[琴晚|Kam4 maan5][瞓唔着|fan3 m4 zoek6]。
lines.id: Since the day before yesterday. I couldn't sleep last night.
lines.literal: day-before-yesterday — open — start. yesterday — night — sleep — not — catch.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [有冇咳呀|Jau5 mou5 kat1 aa3]？[喉嚨痛唔痛|Hau4 lung4 tung3 m4 tung3]？
lines.id: Any cough? Sore throat?
lines.literal: have — not-have — cough — huh. throat — hurt — not — hurt.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [有少少咳|Jau5 siu2 siu2 kat1]，[喉嚨都痛|hau4 lung4 dou1 tung3]。[仲流鼻水|Zung6 lau4 bei6 seoi2]。
lines.id: A bit of a cough, and my throat hurts too. And a runny nose.
lines.literal: have — little — little — cough, throat — also — hurt. still — flow — nose — water.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [有冇肚痛|Jau5 mou5 tou5 tung3]？[有冇嘔呀|Jau5 mou5 au2 aa3]？
lines.id: Any stomachache? Vomiting?
lines.literal: have — not-have — belly — hurt. have — not-have — vomit — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [冇|Mou5]。[但係|Daan6 hai6][冇乜胃口|mou5 mat1 wai6 hau2]。
lines.id: No. But I've got no appetite.
lines.literal: not-have. but — not-have — much — stomach — mouth.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [你有冇藥物敏感呀|Nei5 jau5 mou5 joek6 mat6 man5 gam2 aa3]？
lines.id: Are you allergic to any medicine?
lines.literal: you — have — not-have — medicine — thing — sensitive — feel — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [冇|Mou5]。[嚴唔嚴重呀|Jim4 m4 jim4 zung6 aa3]？
lines.id: No. Is it serious?
lines.literal: not-have. severe — not — severe — serious — huh.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [唔嚴重|M4 jim4 zung6]，[係傷風|hai6 soeng1 fung1]。[你應該休息兩日|Nei5 jing1 goi1 jau1 sik1 loeng5 jat6]，[飲多啲水|jam2 do1 di1 seoi2]。
lines.id: Not serious, just a cold. You should rest for two days and drink plenty of water.
lines.literal: not — severe — serious, is — hurt — wind. you — should — rest — two — day, drink — more — a-bit — water.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [要唔要食藥呀|Jiu3 m4 jiu3 sik6 joek6 aa3]？[可唔可以畀張病假紙我呀|Ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bei2 zoeng1 beng6 gaa3 zi2 ngo5 aa3]？
lines.id: Do I need medicine? Could I get a sick note?
lines.literal: need — not — need — eat — medicine — huh. can — not — can — give — classifier — sick — leave — paper — me — huh.

lines.speaker: 醫生:
lines.text: [冇問題|Mou5 man6 tai4]。[藥一日食三次|Joek6 jat1 jat6 sik6 saam1 ci3]，[飯後食|faan6 hau6 sik6]。[唔好飲凍嘢|M4 hou2 jam2 dung3 je5]。
lines.id: No problem. Take the medicine three times a day, after meals. Don't drink anything cold.
lines.literal: not-have — problem. medicine — one — day — eat — three — times, rice — after — eat. don't — drink — cold — stuff.

notes: **[唔舒服|m4 syu1 fuk6] is the umbrella word for “not feeling well”.** Remember [舒服|syu1 fuk6] from Unit 8. [邊度唔舒服呀|Bin1 dou6 m4 syu1 fuk6 aa3]？ is the doctor's opening question, and it almost never changes.

**⚠️ [痛|tung3] is an adjective, not a noun, so the order is body part + 痛.** [我頭痛|Ngo5 tau4 tung3] = I have a headache — literally “I head hurt”. There's no 我有頭痛 (“I have a headache”); Cantonese adjectives stand on their own, as you learned in Unit 8.
**[發燒|faat3 siu1] = to have a fever, [咳|kat1] = to cough, [流鼻水|lau4 bei6 seoi2] = to have a runny nose.** They're all verbs, not nouns: [我發燒|Ngo5 faat3 siu1] = I have a fever. Again, there's no 我有發燒.

**[瞓唔着|fan3 m4 zoek6] = can't sleep.** [着|zoek6] after 瞓 means actually falling asleep. The verb + 唔 + result pattern you've known since Unit 5: [睇唔到|tai2 m4 dou2], [食唔晒|sik6 m4 saai3], [瞓唔着|fan3 m4 zoek6].
**[冇乜胃口|mou5 mat1 wai6 hau2] = no appetite.** [冇乜|mou5 mat1] = “not much”: [冇乜錢|mou5 mat1 cin2] (not much money), [冇乜時間|mou5 mat1 si4 gaan3] (not much time).
**[敏感|man5 gam2] = both allergic and sensitive.** [藥物敏感|joek6 mat6 man5 gam2] = drug allergy. ⚠️ This is a question you must understand and must answer honestly, so learn the whole question by heart.
**[應該|jing1 goi1] = should, ought to.** It's softer than [要|jiu3] (must). Doctors use 應該 to give advice; warning signs use [唔可以|m4 ho2 ji5] to forbid.
**[飲多啲水|jam2 do1 di1 seoi2] = drink more water.** The pattern verb + [多啲|do1 di1] / [少啲|siu2 di1] = more / less. [瞓多啲|fan3 do1 di1] (sleep more), [食少啲|sik6 siu2 di1] (eat less).

grammars.title: Telling, advising, forbidding
body: Four levels, from the softest to the strongest. What decides it isn't your tone of voice but the word you choose.

head: Level
Word
Example
rows: [不如休息下啦|Bat1 jyu4 jau1 sik1 haa5 laa1]。 Why not take a rest?
[最好唔好出街|Zeoi3 hou2 m4 hou2 ceot1 gaai1]。 Better not go out.
[你應該睇醫生|Nei5 jing1 goi1 tai2 ji1 sang1]。 You should see a doctor.
[你一定要食藥|Nei5 jat1 ding6 jiu3 sik6 joek6]。 You must take your medicine.
[唔使擔心|M4 sai2 daam1 sam1]。 No need to worry.
[唔好飲凍嘢|M4 hou2 jam2 dung3 je5]。 Don't drink anything cold.
[呢度唔可以食煙|Ni1 dou6 m4 ho2 ji5 sik6 jin1]。 No smoking here.

after: ⚠️ **“Don't” is [唔好|m4 hou2], not 唔要.** [唔好走|M4 hou2 zau2] = don't go. 唔要走 doesn't exist. Remember too that 唔好 before an adjective means “not good” — what follows tells them apart.
🇭🇰 **A shorter “don't”: [咪|mai5].** [咪走|Mai5 zau2] = don't go; [咪咁講|Mai5 gam2 gong2] = don't say that. It sounds more casual and quicker, and is used a lot between friends.
**[唔使|m4 sai2] removes an obligation; it doesn't forbid.** [唔使去|M4 sai2 heoi3] = no need to go (you can if you want). [唔好去|M4 hou2 heoi3] = don't go (seriously).

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — At the pharmacy, and a friend's advice
dialogs.intro: Wong Lai goes with Andi to the 藥房. This conversation is full of advice — notice how many different forms are used to say the same thing.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你面色好差|Nei5 min6 sik1 hou2 caa1][喎|wo3]。[食咗藥未呀|Sik6 zo2 joek6 mei6 aa3]？
lines.id: You look really pale, you know. Have you taken any medicine yet?
lines.literal: you — face — color — filler — bad — you-know. eat — already — medicine — not-yet — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [仲未|Zung6 mei6]。[我想買啲咳藥水|Ngo5 soeng2 maai5 di1 kat1 joek6 seoi2]。
lines.id: Not yet. I want to buy some cough syrup.
lines.literal: still — not-yet. I — want — buy — some — cough — medicine — water.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [藥房喺前面|Joek6 fong4 hai2 cin4 min6]。[你唔好行咁快|Nei5 m4 hou2 haang4 gam3 faai3]，[慢慢啦|maan6 maan2 laa1]。
lines.id: The pharmacy's just ahead. Don't walk so fast, take it slow.
lines.literal: medicine — house — at — front — side. you — don't — walk — so — fast, slow — slow — go-on.

lines.speaker: 藥劑師:
lines.text: [要咩藥呀|Jiu3 me1 joek6 aa3]？
lines.id: What do you need?
lines.literal: need — what — medicine — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我傷風|Ngo5 soeng1 fung1]，[有咳|jau5 kat1]，[喉嚨痛|hau4 lung4 tung3]。[有冇藥介紹呀|Jau5 mou5 joek6 gaai3 siu6 aa3]？
lines.id: I've got a cold, a cough and a sore throat. Anything you'd recommend?
lines.literal: I — hurt — wind, have — cough, throat — hurt. have — not-have — medicine — intro — recommend — huh.

lines.speaker: 藥劑師:
lines.text: [呢支咳藥水|Ni1 zi1 kat1 joek6 seoi2][同呢啲喉糖|tung4 ni1 di1 hau4 tong2]。[一日三次|Jat1 jat6 saam1 ci3]。
lines.id: This cough syrup and these throat lozenges. Three times a day.
lines.literal: this — classifier — cough — medicine — water — and — these — some — throat — candy. one — day — three — times.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [食完會唔會眼瞓㗎|Sik6 jyun4 wui5 m4 wui5 ngaan5 fan3 gaa3]？[我要返工|Ngo5 jiu3 faan1 gung1]。
lines.id: Will it make me drowsy? I have to work.
lines.literal: eat — finish — will — not — will — eye — sleep — emphasis. I — must — return — work.

lines.speaker: 藥劑師:
lines.text: [會有少少|Wui5 jau5 siu2 siu2]。[如果要揸車|Jyu4 gwo2 jiu3 zaa1 ce1]，[就唔好食|zau6 m4 hou2 sik6]。
lines.id: A little. If you need to drive, don't take it.
lines.literal: will — have — little — little. if — need — hold — vehicle, then — don't — eat.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [佢唔揸車㗎|Keoi5 m4 zaa1 ce1 gaa3]。[但係你今日唔好返工喇|Daan6 hai6 nei5 gam1 jat6 m4 hou2 faan1 gung1 laa3]，[真係|zan1 hai6]。
lines.id: He doesn't drive. But you shouldn't go to work today, seriously.
lines.literal: he — not — hold — vehicle — emphasis. but — you — this — day — don't — return — work — already, really — is.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我知喇|Ngo5 zi1 laa3]。[我返去瞓覺|Ngo5 faan1 heoi3 fan3 gaau3]。
lines.id: OK, OK. I'll go home and sleep.
lines.literal: I — know — already. I — return — go — sleep.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [記住飲多啲水|Gei3 zyu6 jam2 do1 di1 seoi2]。[保重呀|Bou2 zung6 aa3]！
lines.id: Remember to drink lots of water. Take care!
lines.literal: remember — keep — drink — more — a-bit — water. keep — weighty — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [多謝你|Do1 ze6 nei5]。[你真係好朋友|Nei5 zan1 hai6 hou2 pang4 jau5]。
lines.id: Thanks. You really are a good friend.
lines.literal: thank — you. you — really — are — good — friend.

notes: **[面色|min6 sik1] = complexion, and [面色好差|min6 sik1 hou2 caa1] means you look pale or unwell.** 🇭🇰 It's a normal thing to say to a friend in Hong Kong, and it's taken as caring, not rude.
**[差|caa1] = bad, poor quality.** Its opposite is [好|hou2]. ⚠️ Don't confuse it with [差唔多|caa1 m4 do1] (about the same) from Unit 8 — same character, different expression.

**[慢慢|maan6 maan2] = slowly, take your time.** Note how the tone changes on the second syllable — the tone-change habit explained in the opening chapter. This doubled form also shows up in [快啲快啲|faai3 di1 faai3 di1] (hurry up) and [靜靜哋|zing6 zing2 dei2] (quietly).
**[介紹|gaai3 siu6] = to introduce, to recommend.** [有冇…介紹呀|Jau5 mou5 … gaai3 siu6 aa3]？ = any … you'd recommend? Handy at the pharmacy, the bookshop and restaurants.

**[如果|jyu4 gwo2] = if, and its partner is [就|zau6].** [如果落雨，就唔好去|Jyu4 gwo2 lok6 jyu5, zau6 m4 hou2 heoi3] = if it rains, don't go. 就 goes before the verb in the second clause, and it's almost always there.
**[眼瞓|ngaan5 fan3] = sleepy**, literally “eyes sleep”. A native Cantonese word that doesn't exist in Mandarin. [好眼瞓|hou2 ngaan5 fan3] = really sleepy.
**[揸車|zaa1 ce1] = to drive.** [揸|zaa1] means to grip. Another word with 揸: [揸住|zaa1 zyu6] (keep holding).

**[保重|bou2 zung6] = take care.** Said to someone who's ill or going far away. Other wishes: [早日康復|zou2 jat6 hong1 fuk6] (get well soon, a bit formal) and [好返啲未呀|Hou2 faan1 di1 mei6 aa3]？ (feeling any better?).

grammars.title: 如果 … 就 … and other linking pairs
body: Cantonese links two parts of a sentence with a pair of words, both of them spoken — unlike English, where one word is usually enough.

head: Pair
Meaning
Example
rows: [如果唔舒服，就唔好返工|Jyu4 gwo2 m4 syu1 fuk6, zau6 m4 hou2 faan1 gung1]。
[因為發燒，所以請假|Jan1 wai6 faat3 siu1, so2 ji5 cing2 gaa3]。
[雖然食咗藥，但係都仲痛|Seoi1 jin4 sik6 zo2 joek6, daan6 hai6 dou1 zung6 tung3]。
[一食完藥就眼瞓|Jat1 sik6 jyun4 joek6 zau6 ngaan5 fan3]。
[先食飯然後食藥|Sin1 sik6 faan6 jin4 hau6 sik6 joek6]。

after: ⚠️ **[就|zau6] can rarely be dropped.** [如果落雨唔好去|jyu4 gwo2 lok6 jyu5 m4 hou2 heoi3] sounds cut off; the natural version is [如果落雨，就唔好去|Jyu4 gwo2 lok6 jyu5, zau6 m4 hou2 heoi3].
🇭🇰 **In fast speech, [如果|jyu4 gwo2] is often dropped and only 就 remains.** [唔舒服就唔好返工|M4 syu1 fuk6 zau6 m4 hou2 faan1 gung1] = if you're not well, don't go to work. This is the form you'll hear most.

blocks.title: Six sentences you need to say without thinking
items: [我唔舒服|Ngo5 m4 syu1 fuk6]。 — I'm not feeling well.
[我頭痛|Ngo5 tau4 tung3]，[仲發緊燒|zung6 faat3 gan2 siu1]。 — I have a headache and a fever.
[前日開始㗎|Cin4 jat6 hoi1 ci2 gaa3]。 — It started the day before yesterday.
[我冇藥物敏感|Ngo5 mou5 joek6 mat6 man5 gam2]。 — I have no drug allergies.
[附近有冇診所呀|Fu6 gan6 jau5 mou5 can2 so2 aa3]？ — Is there a clinic nearby?
[叫白車|Giu3 baak6 ce1]！ — Call an ambulance! 🇭🇰 [白車|baak6 ce1] is literally “white car”, and the emergency number is **999**.

sections.title: Seeing a doctor in Hong Kong

head: Place / thing
Cantonese
Note
rows: Private clinic, walk in, medicine included in the fee
Long waits unless it's a real emergency
Green sign; the pharmacist can suggest over-the-counter medicine
Ask the doctor for one; used for work
Its opposite is [西藥|sai1 joek6], Western medicine

blocks.title: Dosage instructions on the packet
items: [一日三次|jat1 jat6 saam1 ci3] — three times a day
[飯後食|faan6 hau6 sik6] — take after meals · [飯前食|faan6 cin4 sik6] — before meals
[每次一粒|mui5 ci3 jat1 nap1] — one tablet each time
[有需要時食|jau5 seoi1 jiu3 si4 sik6] — take as needed
⚠️ [唔好同酒一齊食|M4 hou2 tung4 zau2 jat1 cai4 sik6] — do not take with alcohol

blocks.title: Asking after someone who's ill
items: [好返啲未呀|Hou2 faan1 di1 mei6 aa3]？ — Feeling any better?
[睇咗醫生未呀|Tai2 zo2 ji1 sang1 mei6 aa3]？ — Have you seen a doctor yet?
[記得食藥呀|Gei3 dak1 sik6 joek6 aa3]。 — Remember to take your medicine.
[保重|Bou2 zung6]。 / [早日康復|Zou2 jat6 hong1 fuk6]。 — Take care. / Get well soon.

wave: Five minutes before Unit 12: imagine you're sitting in front of a Hong Kong doctor and play out the whole conversation yourself — what hurts, since when, other symptoms, allergies. Then give five pieces of advice to a friend who's ill, each in a different form: 不如, 最好, 應該, 一定要 and 唔好. If all five come out without a pause, you're ready for the last unit.
